question: ACCELERATOR_TWO_MORE_LEVERS_DIE eliminated six levers and named ONE structural feature no arm had varied: 'the cross-lane reduction tail -- 64 lanes write threadgroup slots and ONE lane serially sums 64 of them while 63 idle. It is INSIDE the previous block's no-weights control too, so that control cannot separate it ... what would settle it: a variant whose reduction is a simd_sum or a tree, holding the element count fixed -- one arm, and it is not run here.' RUN HERE, and with a fourth arm the previous block did not name, which is what actually ends the question.
why_a_deletion_control_and_not_only_the_: Comparing simd_sum and a tree against the serial tail can only say which tail is best. It CANNOT say whether ANY tail matters, because all three still reduce. Deleting the tail entirely bounds what every possible reduction variant can buy: if removing the reduction outright buys nothing, no reduction can. That is a stronger statement than any comparison among the three, and it is the arm that closes the candidate rather than ranking it.
why_the_deletion_control_stores_from_eve: A store predicated on lane==0 lets the compiler SINK the whole loop into the branch -- the loop is pure and its value is used only there -- so 63 lanes would do NO WORK and the arm would read as a ~64x win measuring dead-code elimination. The unconditional store cannot be sunk, and the measurement confirms the guard worked: the arm lands at 301.5 and 302.3 G elem/s, ON the element floor, not 64x above it. It ADDS 64-fold store traffic (4.4 MB against 17408 x 4 B), which makes the bound CONSERVATIVE -- a tie means the tail is worth at most the tie MINUS those extra stores.
what_makes_the_arms_comparable: The body is BYTE-IDENTICAL across all four sources and a test asserts it: same loop, same groups, same fused multiply-adds, so the ELEMENT COUNT is identical and a difference is the tail and nothing else. The shipped NATIVE_MATVEC_TPR is now a composition of that body and the serial tail, pinned byte-identical so the split cannot drift from what executes.

THE_SHIPPED_LOUD_BARRIER_PRIOR_IS_REFUTE.what_it_predicted: kernel_forge.barrier_control_prior returned expected_p_fired = 1.000 with range (1.0, 1.0) and verdict LOUD_CONTROL for this kernel: no upstream barrier, 19 statements since. ACCELERATOR_BARRIER_WINDOW retracted the QUIET number and KEPT the loud one, writing 'the LOUD case is a reliable prediction, since with no upstream barrier EVERY CELL EVER MEASURED fires 1.00'.
THE_SHIPPED_LOUD_BARRIER_PRIOR_IS_REFUTE.verdict: REFUTED. The same kernel measures p = 1.00 and p = 0.067 in different processes, so the LOUD case is as unstable as the QUIET one and the asymmetry that block encoded does not survive contact with a shipped kernel.
THE_SHIPPED_LOUD_BARRIER_PRIOR_IS_REFUTE.the_mechanism_the_prior_cannot_see: A race window is also closed when THE READING THREAD IS THE SLOWEST ONE. Lanes divide 80 groups round-robin over 64 lanes, so lanes 0-15 do two groups and lanes 16-63 do one -- and lane 0, the lane that reads every slot, is in the group doing the MOST work. It arrives at its read after the lanes it reads from have long since written. That is a property of the WORK DISTRIBUTION ACROSS LANES; the prior reads the source's BARRIER STRUCTURE and cannot see it. Reported as a named blind spot rather than folded into a verdict.
THE_SHIPPED_LOUD_BARRIER_PRIOR_IS_REFUTE.a_candidate_named_and_NOT_claimed: run 1 fired 8/8 at 230-259% round-spread and run 2 fired 1/8 at 16-24%, so CONTENTION opening the window is a plausible driver -- n=2 processes, POST-HOC, and it is recorded as a candidate, not a finding.
THE_SHIPPED_LOUD_BARRIER_PRIOR_IS_REFUTE.shipped: CONTROL_LOUDNESS_PRIOR['no_upstream_barrier'] moves 1.000 -> None, expected_p_fired is None in BOTH cases with LOUD_OBSERVED_RANGE = (0.067, 1.000) beside it, and blind_to_lane_work_imbalance is a first-class field. The test that asserted 1.0 now asserts None and carries the refutation in its comment, so nobody re-derives the retracted number.
